title: COVID-19 Lockdown Drives Spain's Deepest Recession on Record
reason: Core event confirmed: Spain's economy did collapse in Q2 2020 due to COVID lockdowns, and 2020 was Spain's worst annual recession in modern records. INE's flash estimate (published 31 July 2020) put Q2 2020 QoQ GDP contraction at -18.5% (later revised to -17.8% in the Sept 2020 second estimate), matching the description almost exactly, and the final full-year 2020 GDP contraction was -11.2/-11.3% (multiple INE vintages), matching "roughly 11 percent." However, the description's specific regional figures for the Balearic and Canary Islands are materially wrong. Per INE's official Contabilidad Regional de España (Regional Accounts) press release (19 Dec 2022, covering the 2019-2021 series), the 2020 GDP decline in volume terms was -23.2% for Illes Balears and -19.1% for Canarias (nominal-terms tables in the same release show -22.8% and -18.2% respectively). An earlier (Dec 2021) vintage cited elsewhere put them at roughly -21.7% and -18.1%. None of these vintages/measures come close to the description's claimed "19.6%" (Balearic) and especially "14.1%" (Canary) — the Canary Islands figure in particular understates the actual regional GDP collapse by roughly 4-5 percentage points (actual ~18-19% vs claimed 14.1%), and Balearic is understated by ~2-3.5 points. Country and year hold, and the top-line national narrative is accurate, but the specific magnitude detail for the two named regions is off enough to be material, so PARTIAL rather than TRUE.
